query: We are investigating the atomic-scale thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt high-entropy alloy (HENA) nanoparticles synthesized via pulsed laser deposition on a silicon nitride membrane. The prevailing hypothesis is that high entropy and sluggish diffusion stabilize the FCC structure against coalescence and segregation. However, in situ heating experiments reveal a progressive loss of sub-5 nm particles and a widening of the size distribution, alongside a reshaping from elliptical to spherical geometries. Theoretical models based on Gibbs free energy often neglect surface energy terms critical for sub-10 nm systems. It has been observed that the FCC structure in these PLD-grown NPs may be governed by kinetic effects rather than entropy. Propose a mechanism explaining why atomic diffusion is surprisingly active in this quinary system, leading to the segregation of specific elements (like Au and Cu) to the surface and subsequent evaporation. Identify the critical temperature threshold where this mechanism becomes dominant, establish the boundary conditions regarding the initial nanoparticle shape (icosahedral vs. truncated octahedron), and formulate a falsification experiment involving simultaneous in situ STEM and atomistic simulations to test if surface energy gradients alone can explain the observed phase separation without invoking sluggish diffusion.

generation.hypothesis: In AuCoCuNiPt high-entropy alloy nanoparticles, surface energy gradients driven by the low cohesive energy of Au and Cu override the sluggish diffusion effect, causing rapid surface segregation and evaporation of these elements above a critical temperature threshold of ~800 K, with the rate of this process being highly sensitive to the initial particle shape (icosahedral vs. truncated octahedron) due to differences in surface atom coordination and curvature.
generation.material_initial_state: Sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles with elliptical geometry, synthesized via pulsed laser deposition on a silicon nitride membrane, possessing a metastable FCC structure governed by kinetic effects rather than thermodynamic entropy stabilization.
generation.intervention: In situ heating of the nanoparticles to temperatures ranging from 300 K to 1200 K under vacuum or inert atmosphere conditions.
generation.conditions: Temperature range 800–1200 K; particle size < 5 nm; initial shapes: elliptical (high surface area/curvature) vs. truncated octahedron (low surface area/curvature); environment: vacuum/inert gas.
generation.structural_mediator: Surface energy gradients and local curvature-induced chemical potential differences, which lower the activation energy for surface diffusion of Au and Cu compared to bulk diffusion.
generation.mechanism: At temperatures exceeding ~800 K, the high surface-to-volume ratio amplifies the thermodynamic driving force for surface segregation of low-surface-energy elements (Au, Cu). Unlike bulk sluggish diffusion, surface diffusion is activated by the high surface energy of the FCC lattice and the specific coordination environment of the initial shape (e.g., high-index facets in elliptical particles), leading to rapid enrichment of Au/Cu at the surface followed by evaporation due to their lower cohesive energies compared to Pt/Ni/Co.
generation.predicted_outcome: Progressive loss of Au and Cu from the nanoparticle surface, resulting in a widening of the size distribution, a transition from elliptical to spherical geometries (minimizing surface energy), and a core-shell structure enriched in Pt/Ni/Co. The rate of this transformation will be significantly faster for elliptical particles compared to truncated octahedrons due to higher surface curvature and defect density.
generation.baseline: The prevailing hypothesis that high entropy and sluggish diffusion stabilize the FCC structure and prevent segregation/coalescence up to 1000 K.
generation.boundary: The mechanism is dominant only for particles < 10 nm where surface energy terms dominate Gibbs free energy; it is suppressed in bulk alloys or particles > 20 nm where bulk diffusion kinetics (sluggish diffusion) remain the rate-limiting step.
generation.uncertainty: The exact critical temperature threshold (predicted ~800 K) is uncertain due to the lack of direct experimental data on AuCoCuNiPt surface diffusion coefficients; the specific contribution of the initial shape (icosahedral vs. truncated octahedron) to the activation energy barrier is not quantified in the available evidence.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform simultaneous in situ STEM heating and atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles of identical composition but distinct initial shapes (elliptical vs. truncated octahedron). The simulations will explicitly calculate surface energy gradients and diffusion barriers for Au/Cu without invoking magnetic entropy or sluggish diffusion terms, while the experiment will measure elemental composition changes via EELS at 10 K intervals from 300 K to 1200 K.
measurements: Real-time elemental mapping (Au, Cu, Co, Ni, Pt) via EELS
Surface diffusion coefficients derived from MD simulations
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if: (1) No significant segregation of Au/Cu is observed up to 1200 K despite the predicted threshold; (2) The rate of shape evolution and size loss is identical for elliptical and truncated octahedral particles, indicating shape-independent kinetics; or (3) MD simulations show that surface energy gradients alone are insufficient to overcome the activation barrier for diffusion without the inclusion of magnetic entropy or bulk sluggish diffusion terms.

cited_evidence.text: Intervention effect. Base system: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating on a single crystal Cu matrix. Intervention: Temperature increased from 300 K to 1200 K. Processing: Molecular dynamics friction simulation; temperature controlled via Nosé–Hoover method. Test conditions: Friction simulation at 300 K and 1200 K. Structure change: Disorder of the lattice structure increases; large number of disordered structures appeared and began to melt. Property change: Friction coefficient increased; tangential force increased. Mechanism: With the increase of temperature, the disorder of the lattice structure increases, which leads to an increase of the tangential force and friction coefficient in the friction process. Evidence: simulated. Quote: "The results show that with the increase of temperature, the disorder of the lattice structure increases, which leads to an increase of the tangential force and friction coefficient in the friction process."

Intervention effect. Base system: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi HEA. Intervention: Stationary friction processing (SFP) at 1800 rpm. Processing: Stationary friction processing with a WC-cylindrical tool rotated at 1800 rpm for 5 min. Test conditions: Surface free energy measurement via contact angle with water and ethanol. Structure change: Significant increase in grain boundary fraction and surface free energy. Property change: Surface free energy increased by 35.2% (from 61.75 to 83.49 mJ/m²). Mechanism: Increased reactivity of elements and favorable sites for chemisorption of O2 due to high grain boundary density. Evidence: measured. Quote: "There is a 29.8% increase in the SFE of the SFP_400 sample and a 35.2% increase in the SFE of the SFP_1800 sample"

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA). Intervention: Exposure to molten salt leading to surface enrichment. Processing: Immersion in molten salt at 650 °C. Test conditions: 650 °C, molten salt. Structure change: Enrichment of Co and Ni in the near-surface region; depletion of Al and Cr. Property change: Formation of a protective surface layer that acts as a barrier against further oxidation. Mechanism: Reduction of Ni2+, Co2+, and Fe2+ ions to atomic form at the surface, assisted by vacancies created during Al and Cr depletion. Evidence: measured. Quote: "In AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 , it is noted that at 650 °C the concentration of Al, Cr, and to a lesser extent, Fe decreased (depletion), while the concentration of Co and Ni increased (enrichment)"
